subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm sketching a compact but detailed design for a six-wheeled heavy railgun carrier, around 9m long and 3m wide, with a front cab, rear turret-mounted railgun, and four deployable outrigger stabilizer legs with ground pads.

Now I'm working out the skeleton structure and joint hierarchy—wheel spin joints, steering joints on the front axle, outrigger extension joints, turret yaw/pitch, and barrel recoil—along with precise coordinates for axle spacing, wheel radius, cab dimensions, and the barrel's forward-angled stowed position over the cab roof.

I'm settling on an olive-grey military color scheme with dark steel accents, yellow hazard stripes, glowing cyan rail-gun elements, plus decal textures for warning labels, number plates, and a screen. I'll build a box helper function and construct the hull from boxes and sloped frustum shapes, keeping the part budget around 200 pieces.

Starting the builder setup now...

Working out wheel spacing...

Picking axle outward for the spin axis, then building wheel geometry: tire cylinder, tread blocks around the ring, rim hub with bolts, and an inner dish, positioning the wheel so its bottom sits near ground level. Moving to the chassis, I'm laying out frame rails and the lower hull box dimensions.

Continuing to the deck with raised side rails and hazard-striped edges, wheel fenders sitting above each axle, and now shaping the cab -- a sloped nose box, a cabin box, and a windscreen panel to give the front its angled truck profile.

Still shaping cab geometry...

Now adding cab details like the roof sensor dome, light bar, headlights, grille vents, bumper wedge, tow hooks, mirrors, antenna, and exhaust stacks with smoke launchers. Then I'm moving to the rear deck, building the turret ring, yaw joint, turret housing, pitch trunnion, and cradle plates, plus the railgun's breech block and rail structure.

Working out the railgun's capacitor drums, coil rings with glow, muzzle brake, and recoil joint, positioning everything relative to the pitch pivot and deciding the pitch angle convention so the barrel raises correctly. I'm also planning to build all parts first and apply poses afterward, keeping stabiliser legs outside the pitch joint's influence, and now considering the turret's yaw axis direction.

Now I'm figuring out the joint hierarchy: pitch as a child of yaw, with yaw rotating about the vertical axis and pitch rotating about its own local axis. I'm sketching the turret body dimensions -- the drum cylinder, housing box, and cheek plates -- stacking their heights so the gun clears the housing and setting the pivot point at the right vertical position.

I'm placing a capacitor bank and cooling fins behind the turret for ammo/power, connecting them to the turret with curved cyan cables, then laying out four stabilizer outriggers with front and rear joint positions tied to the chassis axles.

Each outrigger gets a horizontal housing beam, a piston leg with inner cylinder and outer sleeve, an octagonal foot pad with a ball joint, a diagonal brace, and hazard-striped bands, all named for front-left, front-right, rear-left, and rear-right positions.

Checking ground contact: foot pads sit just above zero, and I'm tuning the tire geometry so the flat-bottomed polygon tread sinks only slightly below y=0 — a negligible fraction of the vehicle's overall height, so I'll simplify to a 16-sided cylinder tire with radius .62 centered at y=.62.

For the hub and tire orientation, I'll rotate the cylinder 90° so its axis runs along X for the spin joint. Then for surface detail I'm planning texture elements: hazard stripes for leg bands and deck edges, an emblem decal for the cab door and turret, a unit marking like "RC-6" on the side, and a warning label such as "HIGH VOLTAGE".

I'm adding a glowing green radar/display texture on the turret side, skipping a few extra ideas like kill markings, and settling on using nested paint functions for camo (olive/dark olive mottle within a panelled base) plus a custom paint gradient for the tires to simulate dirt near the bottom.

Now I'm sketching out helper functions for building box and cylinder parts, and figuring out the right imports from the builder library — pulling in things like paint, mottle, panelled from the clockwork kit, glow from its own kit, plus mix and noise utilities for blending the dirt and hull colors together.

Working out the gun's geometry next: placing the breech block and twin mounting rails along the barrel axis, calculating offsets so the front rails extend past the cab correctly.

Adding more clamp bars...

Moving on to attach rails and clamps to a recoil joint under the pitch bone, with cheek plates on the yaw bone and elevating ram rods connecting housing to the barrel. Now I'm planning additional vehicle details like bumpers, fenders, side skirts, fuel tank, jerry cans, and stowage boxes between the wheels.

Positioning the cab, wheel arches, and fender boxes relative to the axles — placing wheel centers around x±1.45 outside the hull, adding fender boxes over the wheel tops, and mud flaps trailing behind.

For stowage between axles, I'm sorting out overlap issues with the outrigger arm and settling on smaller toolbox-style containers along the deck sides instead, keeping the main hull spanning roughly z -4.7 to 2.4 at the lower deck height.

Checking the outrigger arm beam position against the wheel clearances at mid and rear axles confirms they clear fine, and the leg pad width at x=±2.0 stays within bounds. Now shifting attention to the hull's front nose geometry.

Now I'm placing the front bumper wedge, headlight lenses, and grille bars, then adding the cab's glass windows at x=±1.17, followed by roof accessories like a lightbar, antenna, and radar dome, and finally positioning the exhaust stacks behind the cab.

I'm also adding a mirrored emblem decal plane on the door sides that reads correctly from outside regardless of left or right orientation, plus a unit marking texture on the turret housing and a warning decal on the cap box.

For details, I'm planning a small glowing green-lined screen texture on the turret rear, figuring out how to wrap hazard stripe textures on short cylindrical sleeve bands without distortion, and reconsidering the long deck edge strips -- since a stretched hazard texture would create oversized stripes, I'm switching to painted diagonal stripe patterns directly on the deck edges instead.

I'm also sketching out the wheel hub caps with a green glow, posing the gun with a slight downward pitch, and assigning joint roles like "leg" for the stabilizer legs so the rig understands their function. Now I'm thinking through color choices before writing the final concise export code.

Setting up the palette with olive, sand, steel, dark, cyan, red, and mud tones, then working out the tire paint using a flat tire color with tread blocks, and defining the hull camo as a layered mottle of olive, dark olive, and sand.

I'm refining the camo pattern using irregular organic patches instead of mottle, then layering panel seams with rivets on top, and adding a dirt overlay that blends mud into the lower portion of the hull based on a noise threshold so it looks weathered rather than uniform.

Now I'm figuring out part budget for the wheels — balancing tread block count, hub bolts, and tire geometry to keep the total under a reasonable limit, then working out the trigonometry to position each tread block radially around the wheel's rotation axis.

With that sorted, I'm moving on to the cables connecting the rear capacitor box to the turret, sweeping them along curved points with dark coloring, then designing the capacitor box itself with cooling fins, glow strips, and a warning panel on the chassis deck.

Now I'm placing a tow hitch and red glow lights at the rear, then working through the turret's yaw mechanism—sizing the base ring to clear the hull, shaping the housing box and ammo drum, and adding a sloped front armor plate for the gun assembly.

I'm checking clearances for the pitch components: positioning the breech box and recoil rails relative to the pitch joint, then adjusting the cheek plates and drum diameters so nothing collides as the gun pivots.

I decide to push the drums further along the recoil axis, past the cheek plates, spacing them at regular intervals with clamps and straps connecting to the rails. With the geometry resolved, I'm ready to write the final code, reusing the rod and sweep helper APIs and mirroring parts across the X axis for symmetry, plus adding small details like an antenna and sensor dome on the turret.

I'm extruding the cab body from a flat outline along the chassis axis, centering it and assigning it to the chassis bone. Then I set up the joint hierarchy with the chassis root raised slightly, pose rotations tipping parts forward with negative angles, and nest the recoil assembly under the pitch joint so poses propagate correctly, finishing with spike shapes for the tow hooks.
